subject: humanities
passage: Many houses in the Faroe Islands are still topped with a thick layer of living ______ a tradition the islanders inherited from Norse settlers more than a thousand years ago. The roof is built up in layers: wooden boards first, then sheets of birch bark to keep water out, and finally squares of turf laid grass side up. The grass holds the soil together, the soil holds in heat, and the whole layer is heavy enough to stay put in the fierce Atlantic winds. In summer, a turf roof needs mowing like any other lawn.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "A tradition the islanders inherited from Norse settlers more than a thousand years ago" is extra information that renames the turf roof; it is not a sentence on its own. An added phrase like this at the end of a sentence is attached with a comma.
explanation.A: Correct. The comma attaches the extra information to the sentence it describes.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Without a comma, the extra information runs straight into the main clause and is never set off.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "A tradition the islanders inherited …" has no verb of its own, so the period leaves a fragment.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A semicolon must have an independent clause on both sides, but "a tradition the islanders inherited …" is not one.
